A simple vertical bar chart comparing the approximate annual rainfall of six Nigerian towns from south to north, with no numbers on the bars. Bars from left to right get shorter: Calabar (tallest, dark blue), Benin City, Makurdi, Kaduna, Kano, Maiduguri (shortest, pale blue). Under each bar, a small icon of its typical vegetation: mangrove or rainforest tree, rainforest tree, tall grass with trees, shorter grass with trees, baobab and Acacia, sparse thorny shrub. A horizontal arrow under the chart pointing right. Soft blues and greens.

Side view (profile) of a Nigerian tropical rainforest showing its layers. A few very tall emergent trees (silk cotton with buttress roots, iroko) rise above a continuous closed canopy of broad-crowned trees. Below: an understorey of smaller trees, a shrub layer, and a dark forest floor with ferns, seedlings and thick leaf litter. Lianas climb up trunks; epiphytic orchids and ferns on branches. Animals: a hornbill and a monkey in the canopy, a chameleon on a branch, a duiker and a giant snail on the forest floor. A height scale on the left in metres (0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50). Light rays strong above the canopy and dim near the floor. Soft greens and browns.

Two side-by-side panels comparing southern and northern Guinea savanna. Left panel (southern Guinea savanna): tall elephant grass over head height, fairly close broad-leaved trees, a gallery forest along a river in the background, a kob antelope, and a yam farm with mounds at the edge. A person for scale. Right panel (northern Guinea savanna): shorter grass about waist-to-chest height, more widely spaced shorter trees with corky bark (Isoberlinia), a termite mound, a herd of white Fulani cattle with a herder, and a sorghum field. Soft greens, yellows and browns.

Landscape of Nigerian Sudan savanna in the dry season. Short, dry, yellow-brown grass about knee-to-waist height; widely scattered short thorny Acacia trees with small leaves and a large baobab with a fat grey trunk and no leaves; a doum palm with a branched trunk. A small millet field with harvested stalks, a mud-walled village with granaries, cattle and goats grazing, a camel, and a hazy dusty sky from the harmattan. Soft yellows, tans and pale blue.

Landscape of the Sahel savanna near Lake Chad in the dry season. Very short, sparse tufts of dry grass with much bare sandy ground between them, a few low thorny Acacia shrubs, a doum palm, a small sand dune creeping over a field edge, a herd of camels and goats with a herder, and the shallow edge of Lake Chad with reeds in the distance. Soft tans, pale yellows and pale blues.

Desert scene with sand dunes and a small oasis. Show: bare sand and rocky ground, a few thorny Acacia shrubs, succulent spiny euphorbias, a clump of date palms around a pool at an oasis, a dromedary camel with a single hump, long eyelashes and broad padded feet, a fennec fox with very large ears at a burrow entrance, a jerboa with long hind legs, a desert locust and a scorpion on the sand. A hot sun in a clear sky. Soft yellows, oranges and pale blues.

Side view of the Obudu Plateau rising steeply from lowland rainforest. At the foot, dense, tall tropical rainforest with a thermometer showing a high reading. Up the steep slopes, montane forest in valleys and along streams, with mist. On the flat plateau top, open rolling montane grassland with short grass, grazing cattle, a few cottages and a cable car line running up the slope. A thermometer at the top showing a lower reading. Inset in a corner: a tea bush with leaves and an Irish potato plant with tubers, representing crops of the Mambilla and Jos Plateaus. Soft greens, blues and browns.

Outline map of Nigeria showing its vegetation belts as coloured bands running roughly west to east. From the south coast northwards: a thin dark-green coastal strip (mangrove and swamp forest, widest in the Niger Delta), a green band (tropical rainforest), a pale green band (derived savanna), a yellow-green band (southern Guinea savanna), a yellow band (northern Guinea savanna, the widest), a pale orange band (Sudan savanna), and a light tan area in the far north-east around Lake Chad and along the northern border (Sahel savanna). Three small brown-purple patches for the highlands: the Jos Plateau in the centre, the Mambilla Plateau on the eastern border, and the Obudu Plateau in the south-east. Dots for main towns: Lagos, Port Harcourt, Calabar, Benin City, Ibadan, Enugu, Ilorin, Makurdi, Abuja, Jos, Kaduna, Zaria, Kano, Sokoto, Maiduguri. Rivers Niger and Benue in blue. An arrow down the side showing "rainfall decreases northwards". A label for the Sahara Desert beyond the northern border. Soft natural colours.
